note: Contrarian Shark, skeptical-researcher angle. Judged only against the locked North Star surfaces, not the elegance table’s attempt to reopen them. Heartbeat at `planning/code-windows-2026-09-07/stage1/artifacts/heartbeat.json`.

findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview (cwd = project folder, OS-assigned port never 8777, own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped)
findings.message: The locked criterion is a per-project lab with preview discipline. The plan still specifies `lab_server.py`, then HOLDs it and every dependent (ensure/probe, fake_lab, labs endpoints, Lab chip, 127.0.0.1 Location) until John picks (A) existing jupyter-serve or (B) a new lab — and says spend zero until (B). Option (A) is not criterion 1: it is not per-project, not cwd = the project folder, not an OS-assigned port, not registered/listed/stoppable/reaped like a preview. A Master Plan that leaves the substrate as a Stage-0 rewrite cannot deliver the surface. The KEEP’d work (classifier, chips, href rewrite) does not make a lab come up.

findings.section: Phase 2 — ensure_lab wait vs immediate interstitial (P3.3 / P3.7 HOLD)
findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The same paragraph requires `ensure_lab` to wait up to 20 s for a probe AND the route to answer IMMEDIATELY with a poll page. It does not say who starts the lab if the wait is not on the request thread, and it HOLDs both the interstitial and `lab_ready` until a recorded hung click. What remains is a blocking 302-after-probe. A cold JupyterLab boot is then a silent 20 s tab — the blank page criterion 2 forbids. Stub `fake_lab` answers at once, so no test in Phases 0–3 ever sees a real boot. Premortem 1 is claimed closed in prose and HOLD’d in the table.

findings.criterion: 2 — opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file (starting the lab if needed)
findings.message: Kind-dispatch is KEEP’d; the Location it 302s to is HOLD’d. If (B), the click goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/…` of a lab the plan is not yet allowed to spawn. If (A), `/lab/tree/<rel>` is relative to jupyter-serve’s root, not the project folder, so an in-effort notebook is a 404 or the wrong tree — and nothing starts or restarts a dead lab. Criterion 2 is one click that lands on that file in that project’s lab. This route as HOLD’d has no such target.

findings.topic: sign-off does not observe the opens
findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected, a short .py opens as a notebook, a long .py opens in the editor, a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: The four screenshots do not measure the four claims. (a) “file selected” is a document title or tab-label `or`, which a JupyterLab shell with the path only in the URL can satisfy. (c) asserts a `vscode://file/` navigation while criterion 3 names `code -r <file>` and P3.5 HOLDs the URI handler — so the live gate proves a path the plan itself parked. (d) asserts `href` has no `token=` and `rel` contains noopener; it never follows the link. The live-link row is `http://gwl-server:<lab port or 8888>/lab` while Phase 1 binds `--ip=127.0.0.1` and `allow_remote_access=False`, so that host:port is not the managed lab (and 8888 is a guess). Criterion 5 is eyes on the opens, not attribute lints plus a PNG.

findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`), and the row says which
findings.message: The locked launcher is `code -r <file>`. The overview, the editor page, and the sign-off all dual-fire `vscode://file/<abs>` plus the seam, which can open the file twice and put an absolute path in history. P3.5 HOLDs the URI half “until a recorded click where `code -r` did not land,” while Phase 4 still requires a `vscode://` href to pass. Criterion 3 is satisfied by a non-blocking `code -r` that actually raises the file. The extra scheme is not in the criterion, and the gate that is supposed to see the editor is wired to the parked half.

findings.topic: tailnet allowlist not durable on the service
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, or this machine's tailnet name renders as a link; every other host stays text
findings.message: Production resolution of “this machine’s tailnet name” is `socket.gethostname()` (this host’s friendly name is not guaranteed to be the tailnet name), plus a 2 s `tailscale status --self --json` subprocess, plus an unset `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. Tests inject the env and stub the binary. The register is served by the NSSM `anchor` process, whose PATH has already been the reason external CLIs vanish. If the probe fails, `http://gwl-server/…` and the friction-note FQDN stay text — journal 0110 unfixed on the live service. Criterion 4 is a row John can click, not a stubbed frozenset. The allowlist needs a durable, service-visible name list, not a best-effort spawn.

findings.criterion: 3 — short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines)
findings.message: One sentence specifies two incompatible scans: “the first 5 non-blank lines for `# %%`” and “anywhere in the file counts as a cell marker, scanned up to the 121-line cap.” A 100-line file with `# %%` on line 50 is editor under the first rule and notebook under the second. The stub table pins “`# %%` on line 3 of a 400-line file → notebook,” which is a third case (long + marker). P1.1 then HOLDs that third case until John re-ratifies text already in the locked criterion (“short OR marked”). A classifier with two windows and a HOLD on the criterion’s own marker clause will not render the same chip the route executes.

findings.section: Phase 0 — to_notebook (P1.2 KEEP / P1.3 HOLD) and Phase 2 dispatch
findings.criterion: 3 — converted once to a sibling one-cell .ipynb
findings.message: Criterion 3 is one-cell. P1.3 HOLD says omit `marker_split` from the writer, the route, and the tests. P1.2 KEEP still takes `marker_split=False`, the Judge-flag paragraph still tests both paths, and P3.2 still passes `marker_split=<Judge flag>`. A HOLD that leaves the flag on the KEEP’d signature is a split converter Foreman will implement. That is not one-cell, and it is not a cut.

findings.topic: R kernel unproven on the page
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred “R kernel install” / Phase 4 fixture
findings.criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row … kernel python3 or ir; statement — JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
findings.message: The statement requires Python and R kernels in the project lab. The plan writes `ir` into JSON and defers installing or detecting IRkernel. Phase 4’s live list is ipynb / short .py / long .py / live-link; the `.R` row is “skipped honestly if IRkernel is missing.” Criterion 5 was the gate that would have caught a kernel-less R open; it was written to omit R. An `.R` click can therefore ship as a notebook whose kernel is absent — open, not where it runs. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping R as an untested metadata tag is not.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens at /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Files-tile clicks are `window.open` of `/notebook` with `dir=''` and “the path is project-relative there.” The plan does not say the files payload actually carries project-root-relative paths. If a produced file is effort-relative (the register’s `dir` exists for that reason), `dir=''` joins to a path that fails the containment check or 404s, and the files tile is the one surface that never starts the lab on the right file. Criterion 2 names that tile. Register and plan inherit `dir`; files are specified as if they do not need it, without a proof that the producer agrees.

The locked labels are notebook and editor. The chip also prints `lab` for `.ipynb`. That is a third word the criterion does not use, so a notebook row does not “say which” in the vocabulary the surface locked. Harmless if renamed; as specified it fails the letter of criterion 3 on the most common row.
